<p>Agricultural advisory systems often need to combine current observations, earlier visits, and crop-disease knowledge, but existing agricultural benchmarks mainly evaluate image classification or short-form question answering. We present AgriMemSynth, a synthetic benchmark framework for evaluating agricultural question answering under two complementary requirements: multi-session conversational memory and structured multi-hop reasoning. AgriMemSynth provides AgriConvMem, a set of 500 generated advisory conversations, and AgriMultiHop, a set of 2,000 generated reasoning questions. Using held-out test splits with 146 conversational-memory questions and 200 multi-hop questions, we compare five retrieval organizations under a shared answer-generation pipeline: retrieval-augmented generation, a neuroscientific memory system, a hybrid retriever, BM25 with semantic reranking, and a graph-based memory system. Semantic evaluation reveals three stable benchmark patterns. First, lexical metrics substantially underestimate answer correctness. Second, conversational memory is harder than generated multi-hop reasoning. Third, retrieval organization is task-dependent: RAG has the highest conversational-memory score (85.6 %, 95 % CI: 79.0-90.4), whereas MemoryGraph has the highest multi-hop score (97.0 %, 95 % CI: 93.6-98.6). Temporal questions remain the weakest conversational category. These results support AgriMemSynth as a controlled benchmark for studying how agricultural AI systems organize, retrieve, and apply knowledge across longitudinal and relational
